description:
pkix-lint/src/lib.rs:131 declares `use std::borrow::Cow;` at the top of the file. Then in the body — lib.rs:991, 1028, 1060, 1264, 1265, 1366, 1367, and ~15 test-only locations — the fully qualified `std::borrow::Cow::Borrowed(...)` and `std::borrow::Cow<'static, str>` paths are used instead of the imported alias `Cow::Borrowed(...)` / `Cow<'static, str>`. 

No engineering reason for the inconsistency — the alias is in scope. Reading is harder because the eye has to discount the noise prefix on every line. `Cow::Borrowed(lint.id())` vs `std::borrow::Cow::Borrowed(lint.id())` is the difference between 3 and 5 visual tokens to express the same construction.

Fix: replace all `std::borrow::Cow` references in lib.rs with `Cow`. Mechanical change; no test-coverage gap risk.

Note: deviation.rs is consistent the other direction (no `use` and FQ paths throughout). That is also defensible — it's the inconsistency within a single file that's flagged here.
title: std::borrow::Cow::Borrowed fully qualified despite top-level use std::borrow::Cow
